Determine the set of points \((x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2\) at which the function \( f(x, y) \) is continuous, where \( f: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R} \) is defined by:

\[ f(x, y) = \begin{cases} \frac{\varphi(y) - \varphi(x)}{y-x} & x \neq y \\ \varphi'(x) & x = y \end{cases} \]

and \( \varphi : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} \) is a differentiable function with a continuous derivative \( \varphi'(x) \).
Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}.
